gloss: to take a walk; to go for a stroll

definitions.gloss: to take a walk; to go for a stroll
definitions.explanation: To walk leisurely for relaxation, exercise, or enjoyment rather than to reach a specific destination. A common daily activity in Japan, especially for the elderly and dog owners.

examples.japanese: {公園|こうえん}を{散歩|さんぽ}する。
examples.english: To take a walk in the park.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}、{犬|いぬ}と{一緒|いっしょ}に{散歩|さんぽ}している。
examples.english: I go for a walk with my dog every morning.

examples.japanese: {食後|しょくご}に{少|すこ}し{散歩|さんぽ}すると{体|からだ}にいい。
examples.english: Taking a short walk after eating is good for your health.

examples.japanese: {休日|きゅうじつ}は{川沿|かわぞ}いの{道|みち}を{散歩|さんぽ}するのが{楽|たの}しみだ。
examples.english: On days off, I enjoy walking along the riverside path.

notes:
One of the most common daily activities mentioned in Japanese conversation. Taking a {散歩|さんぽ} is considered both a health practice and a form of relaxation. The particle used with locations varies: {公園|こうえん}を{散歩|さんぽ}する (through/around a park) or {公園|こうえん}で{散歩|さんぽ}する (at a park).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {朝|あさ}の{散歩|さんぽ}: morning walk
- {犬|いぬ}の{散歩|さんぽ}: walking the dog
- {散歩|さんぽ}{道|みち}: walking path
- {散歩|さんぽ}コース: walking route
- {散歩|さんぽ}に{行|い}く: to go for a walk

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {歩|ある}く: to walk — neutral verb for the physical action of walking
- ウォーキング: walking (exercise) — implies deliberate exercise with health goals
- {徘徊|はいかい}する: to wander — aimless walking, sometimes with negative connotation
